report_policy.core_research_question: Does the GPT-2 Large finding (layer-0 embedding L2 distance D between ' big' and token B does not visibly predict interpolation transition width W; final layer sharper than middle layer; W_final one broad peak with tail) generalize to GPT2-XL, Pythia 1.4B, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B-Base?

checklist.request: Can you check if the study can be generalized to GPT2-XL, Pythia 1.4B, Llama-3.1-8B，Qwen3-8B-Base

completion.what_was_done: Re-ran the full GPT-2 Large study (prompt 'The house was big', ' big' -> every other token, 101 interpolation steps, W at middle and final block) on GPT2-XL (50,256 tokens), Pythia 1.4B (50,276), Llama-3.1-8B (128,255; weights from ungated mirror unsloth/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B) and Qwen3-8B-Base (151,668). Full vocabularies, 8B models unquantized bf16 with float32 residual stream; precision checked (median |dW_final| 0.002-0.003).
completion.evidence: REPORT_generalization.md (Summary, Methods, Results sections 'GPT2-XL', 'Pythia 1.4B', 'Llama-3.1-8B', 'Qwen3-8B-Base', Figures 1-12); RESULTS_generalization.md G0-G4; results/gen/<model>.csv, results/gen/<model>_summary.json; experiments/gen_common.py, gen_sweep.py, gen_plots.py.

checklist.request: I want you to have one section for each of the models. In each section, reproducing study that made figure 1-3 and S4 tabele. In each section, show the new plots for each model and the part of the table that corresponding to W 0.3

completion.what_was_done: One Results subsection per model. Each reproduces REPORT.md Figure 1 (D vs W scatter, middle and final block), Figure 2 (zoom on the dense core; range = that model's 5th-95th D percentile because D scales differ) and Figure 3 (W_final histogram + sorted view), and shows the 0.30-0.50 W_final row of the RESULTS.md S4 table (token count + 7 lowest-D examples). Full S4-style tables for every band are in RESULTS_generalization.md. Rejection fix 2026-09-28: each band-row description now states only what the lowest-D example column shows (the examples are the band members closest to ' big'), not what the whole band contains; Pythia examples described as case/spacing variants of 'big'.
completion.evidence: REPORT_generalization.md: GPT2-XL = Figures 1-3 + 0.30-0.50 table; Pythia 1.4B = Figures 4-6 + table; Llama-3.1-8B = Figures 7-9 + table; Qwen3-8B-Base = Figures 10-12 + table. plots/gen/<model>_fig{1,2,3}_*.png. Full band tables: RESULTS_generalization.md G1-G4.

checklist.request: Then, in a final section, use several sentences to summarize if the trend can be generalized to those models.

completion.what_was_done: Final section summarizes, with a comparison table, which GPT-2 Large findings generalize: distance does not visibly predict width (all four), final block sharper (GPT2-XL, Pythia, Llama; not Qwen3-8B-Base), one broad peak with tail (all four; peak position model-specific), size words among widest (3 of 4, partly Qwen3). Rejection fix 2026-09-28: removed the unsupported causal sentence linking peak position to the example column (now stated as reflecting each model's low-D tokens, cause not tested); Methods precision paragraph and the Qwen3 section now state that Qwen3's 0.003 median depth gap and 56.2% sharper share are near the bfloat16 rounding error, so only the qualitative 'not clearly sharper' conclusion is claimed.
completion.evidence: REPORT_generalization.md section 'Conclusion — does the trend generalize?' (comparison table + paragraphs); RESULTS_generalization.md G5. Precision caveat: REPORT_generalization.md Methods 'Checking the computation' and Qwen3-8B-Base section after Figure 11.

routing_notes: Interpretations that are NOT blocking (recorded for the next pass): 'figure 1-3' = REPORT.md Figures 1-3 = plots/fig1_distance_vs_width.png (D vs W scatter, middle and final block), plots/fig1_zoom_distance_vs_width.png (zoom D 1.6-3.3), plots/fig2_final_width_distribution.png (W_final histogram + sorted view). 'S4 tabele' = the W_final band table in RESULTS.md section S4 (band, token count, lowest-D examples). 'the part of the table that corresponding to W 0.3' = the '0.30-0.50' W_final band row (the only band containing 0.3), per model. Per-model adaptation: same prompt 'The house was big' with A = that model's ' big' token, B = every other vocabulary id, 101 steps, readouts at the middle block (n_layers/2, analogous to GPT-2 Large block 18 of 36) and the final block (pre final norm), same W and flag definitions. Existing GPT-2 Large results stay unchanged. OPERATOR ROUTING (PLAN.md, 2026-09-28): sections + final synthesis -> REPORT_generalization.md (up to 12 main figures); detailed results -> RESULTS_generalization.md; GPT-2 Large REPORT.md/RESULTS.md unchanged. GPU: per-agent budget is now 0.45 x 31.9 GB = 14.4 GB. 8B models are run UNMODIFIED in their native bf16 weights: prefix keys/values are computed once and only the last position is run; transformer blocks that do not fit on the GPU are copied from CPU memory block-by-block (exact computation, no quantization). This was option (c) of the earlier ambiguity and does not change the model studied. Llama-3.1-8B: the official repo is gated and no HF token exists here; weights are taken from the ungated mirror unsloth/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B (same base-model weights), stated in the report. Pythia: EleutherAI/pythia-1.4b (default). Zoom panel (Figure 2 analogue): GPT-2 Large used D 1.6-3.3; for each new model the zoom range is that model's 5th-95th D percentile.

failures: Claim contradicted by the report's own data (REPORT_generalization.md, Summary, 'Shape' bullet): 'So the 0.30–0.50 band is the tail in the GPT-2 models but typical in the others.' 'The others' includes Llama-3.1-8B. For Llama, RESULTS_generalization.md G3 gives a W_final 90th percentile of 0.308 and a peak at 0.19–0.20. Only 14,583 of 128,255 tokens (about 11%) fall in 0.30–0.50. So for Llama that band sits above the 90th percentile, which makes it the tail, not typical. The Conclusion says this more carefully ('in the tail for the GPT-2 models and typical for Pythia'), so the Summary and Conclusion now disagree. The Summary sentence should be corrected: typical for Pythia, and upper side or tail for Llama. Qwen3 needs its own description too (23% of tokens, 90th percentile 0.374).

Minor inconsistency a new reader could stumble on (REPORT_generalization.md, GPT2-XL section): '11.6% of curves are flagged, almost all at the final block (5.5% in GPT-2 Large)'. This compares an any-block flag rate with a GPT-2 Large figure, while the Conclusion table reports final-block flag rates (11.5% vs 5.3%). Use one definition consistently.
content.summary: All three failures from the previous review are fixed. The GPT2-XL band text now says only what its lowest-D examples show. The causal link between peak position and the example column has been removed and replaced with an explicit statement that the cause was not tested. The precision paragraph and the Qwen3 section now say plainly that Qwen3's depth gap and its 56.2% share are near the bfloat16 rounding error. The structure still does what was asked: one section per model, Figure 1–3 analogues, the 0.30–0.50 S4 row, and a final synthesis. It stays within budget (12 figures, under 5,000 words), and RESULTS is a curated archive rather than a duplicate of the report. It still fails on one factual overclaim. The Summary says the 0.30–0.50 band is 'typical' in Llama, Pythia and Qwen3, but the Llama data (90th percentile 0.308, about 11% of tokens in the band) show it is the tail for Llama. This also contradicts the Conclusion's more careful wording. There is also a smaller inconsistency in how flag rates are compared between models.
